# Gradle Maven-layout repositories

<!-- Generated by tools/clientrecipes from src/gradle.json; edit the source. -->

Read the [common setup and credential rules](README.md) first. [All recipes](index.md).

Client: **Gradle 9.8.2 on Temurin 27; optional JFrog CLI 2.131.0 wrapper**. Registered classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**.

Endpoint: `${AW_URL}/artifactory/${AW_REPO}`

## Before connecting

- Use a gradle repository with repoLayoutRef=maven-2-default, since maven-publish writes Maven paths.
- The checksum-verified Gradle distribution in the pinned Maven client image.

Authentication: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.

Fresh client state: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.

## Configure

Use the pinned Gradle executable. Set repository layout maven-2-default for this Maven publication/resolution recipe. Credentials are read from exported AW_USER/AW_TOKEN. Separate producer and consumer homes when proving an independent download.

```sh
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
export GRADLE_USER_HOME="$AW_WORK/gradle-home"
export AW_REPO_URL="$AW_URL/artifactory/$AW_REPO"
```

## Publish

Classes: **local, federated**. Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

Producer build.gradle; settings.gradle must set rootProject.name = "widget". Place the producer sources/resources under src/main. The endpoint must use HTTPS.

```groovy
plugins { id 'java-library'; id 'maven-publish' }
group = 'org.acme'
version = '1.0.0'
publishing {
    publications { mavenJava(MavenPublication) { from components.java } }
    repositories { maven {
        url = uri(System.getenv('AW_REPO_URL'))
        credentials { username = System.getenv('AW_USER'); password = System.getenv('AW_TOKEN') }
    } }
}
```

Run from the producer project. This is direct Gradle publication; JFrog build-info integration remains a separately recorded informational lane.

```sh
gradle --no-daemon -Duser.home="$AW_WORK/home" publish
```

## Install or resolve

Classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**. Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

Consumer build.gradle in a separate empty project; create settings.gradle with a consumer name. Use a new GRADLE_USER_HOME and project directory.

```groovy
plugins { id 'base' }
repositories { maven {
    url = uri(System.getenv('AW_REPO_URL'))
        credentials { username = System.getenv('AW_USER'); password = System.getenv('AW_TOKEN') }
} }
configurations { recipe }
dependencies { recipe 'org.acme:widget:1.0.0' }
tasks.register('resolveRecipe', Copy) {
    from configurations.recipe
    into 'retrieved'
}
```

Checks the configured repository for the requested module; no mavenLocal() repository is added.

```sh
gradle --no-daemon -Duser.home="$AW_WORK/home" resolveRecipe
```

## Limits

Classes outside **local, remote, virtual, federated** are not registered for this format. Commands above apply only to each operation's listed classes. Federated evidence is for one node; it does not establish cross-vendor replication.

- The historical gradle-default Ivy-style layout needs a different resolver/publication pattern and is not represented by these commands.
- JFrog CLI gradle integration is informational; direct Gradle recipe verification is a required native acceptance scenario.
- The isolated test server uses HTTP loopback and explicitly enables allowInsecureProtocol there; production snippets require HTTPS.
